transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-03-03 15:00 PST | Duration: ~45m
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Chu (Redwood SE), Samir Khan (NovaPay CTO), Lena Ortiz (NovaPay ML Lead), Priya Desai (NovaPay Infra)

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick note on agenda — model selection updates, pinning strategy, and rollout / fallback plan. we'll also go over the latest perf numbers Ethan pulled.
[00:18] Samir: yeah thanks, Maya. we' re mainly looking to decide which model to lock for the pilot. our QA is seeing some drift on the LLM outputs and we hit token cost concerns, so want to weigh latency vs cost.
[00:30] Maya: perfect. Ethan, can you give the recap of the benchmark?
[00:34] Ethan: sure, quick summary — we tested three catalog candidates from Redwood: meta-llama-2-13b@v1.3.2 (non-quant), mistral-7b-instruct@v2.0, and redwood/gpt-jr-13b@v1.1-quant. baseline was hosted; we also ran on Dedicated with reserved GPUs. overall accuracy (intent/exact-match) was highest on the llama 13b, latency P95 on Dedicated was 220ms for the 13b non-quant, 140ms for mistral-7b, and 95ms for the quantized gpt-jr variant. cost per 1k tokens was roughly $3.40, $1.80, and $0.95 respectively on our pricing assumptions.
[01:12] Lena: quick clarification — the accuracy delta between llama and mistral looked like 3.6% absolute on our eval prompts, right?
[01:18] Ethan: yeah correct, on the 1.2k prompt set used in the eval harness. note though the llama had fewer hallucinations for our payment reconciliation prompts.
[01:28] Priya: cost matters but also deterministic behavior for compliance — if we go quantized we need to ensure we have consistent outputs and reproducible rollbacks. how do you handle pin+rollback?
[01:38] Maya: good q. Redwood supports explicit model pinning in the Console — you can pin by model id + version tag (e.g., meta-llama-2-13b@v1.3.2). we also recommend configuring a fallback map: if the pinned version fails, route to a compatible variant (for example v1.2.8 or a quantized compatible build). rollbacks are automated via the rollout policy or you can force a rollback from the Console.
[01:56] Samir: is the fallback instant? i mean, we can't have large cold-starts that spike latency during failover.
[02:03] Ethan: fallback is near-instant at the routing layer — we match by semantic compatibility and hardware availability. cold-start risk exists if the fallback is on a different hardware class; we recommend pre-warming the fallback pool in Dedicated. the Console lets you maintain a warm standby.
[02:18] Priya: pre-warming sounds needed. on VPC deployment what are the constraints for pre-warm? does it eat into reserved capacity?
[02:25] Ethan: pre-warm uses reserved Dedicated capacity if you configure it there; for Private on-prem you can follow the pre-warm scripts we shared. it will count against the pool, yes, so we size the Dedicated commit to include a small warm buffer.
[02:36] Maya: back to model selection — thoughts? the tradeoff is accuracy (llama) vs latency/cost (mistral or quantized gpt-jr). Samir, what is your primary success metric for the pilot?
[02:48] Samir: two things: 1) <98% reconciliation match on our validation set and 2) P95 latency under 300ms on Dedicated with 95% of traffic. cost target is softer — keep under our current per-user token budget.
[03:04] Lena: on the evaluation, if we hit 98% match with the llama but at 220ms P95, that's within Samir's latency SLO. cost is higher though. we could try an A/B: 80% traffic to llama, 20% to mistral as a candidate, with continuous quality checks.
[03:18] Maya: that's exactly what Redwood's rollout can do — canaries and traffic-weighted rollouts per route, and automatic quality regression detection via your prompt sets. we can wire your evaluation callbacks so the Console will alert if mismatch rate increases.
[03:33] Samir: good. about version pinning — Lena suggested pin to v1.3.2 for a week and then reassess, is that operationally easy?
[03:41] Ethan: yes, pin+monitor is straightforward. we recommend pinning the model id plus a signed artifact (we surface the model checksum in the Console) so you can audit exact bytes. if you want to move to a newer version, you can create a staged rollout to v1.3.3 with canary traffic and automatic rollback on quality regression.
[03:58] Priya: audit logs are important for us. where do we get those?
[04:02] Maya: audit logs and token-level traces are in Redwood Console and we can export to your SIEM. SOC 2 and ISO attestation docs are in the security pack we'll share.
[04:12] Samir: Ethan, you mentioned quantized variant stability — can you expand? we worry quantized models sometimes change behavior subtly.
[04:20] Ethan: absolutely. quantization can shift logits and cause small output changes; for many tasks it's acceptable but for reconciliation we saw a slight bump in false positives in the quantized gpt-jr tests. we recommend using quantization for high-throughput fallbacks or lower criticality routes, and keep non-quant (or higher-precision) for the main reconciliation flow. Redwood Optimize can recommend per-route quantization profiles.
[04:43] Lena: does Redwood provide automated mapping for compatible fallbacks? like if we pin meta-llama-2-13b@v1.3.2, can the system automatically select meta-llama-2-13b@v1.2.8-quant as fallback?
[04:53] Ethan: yes, you can define a compatibility map in the routing policy or use the default 'compatible_variants' rule where we match by schema/arch tag. the Console UI shows compatibility warnings if the fallback differs in topology (e.g., 13b -> 7b).
[05:06] Maya: quick note: because you have sensitive PII in some prompts, we should confirm data residency—NovaPay is on a EU region for hosted?
[05:12] Samir: we need EU for production. pilot can run in hosted NA but for compliance we want Private or Dedicated in eu-west1 later.
[05:20] Priya: also SSO and KMS — we need KMS integration for key management with HSM option and SAML SSO.
[05:27] Maya: we'll include the KMS/HSM integration checklist in the security pack. we support customer-managed keys in Dedicated and Private.
[05:34] Samir: ok next, run cadence — Lena, are you okay to sign off on the prompt set and accuracy thresholds by next Friday?
[05:40] Lena: yes i can finalize the 1.2k prompt set and annotated expected outputs by 2025-03-07.
[05:46] Maya: great. proposed pilot plan from Redwood: pin meta-llama-2-13b@v1.3.2 as primary, configure a mistral-7b-instruct@v2.0 canary at 10% for quality guardrails, keep redwood/gpt-jr-13b@v1.1-quant as a low-latency fallback for non-critical routes. pre-warm fallback pool on Dedicated and run a scheduled perf run 2025-03-12.
[06:08] Samir: sounds reasonable. what about cost mitigation? can we use partial caching? we have a decent prompt overlap for reconciliation tasks.
[06:16] Ethan: yes, enable prefix/KV caching for repeated templates; that drops token costs significantly. Redwood's runtime supports automatic prefix caching and we can surface hot keys in Console. caching is safe for deterministic prompts, but be careful with prompts containing user-specific PII — you can set caching rules per-route.
[06:31] Priya: do we need any infra changes to enable caching in our VPC Dedicated setup?
[06:36] Ethan: just a config flag and optional Redis-backed shared KV if you want cross-instance cache persistence; we can handle it in the Dedicated pool without extra infra if you want ephemeral cache only.
[06:45] Lena: one more note: in the last run we saw a spike at 2pm during our sim load — P99 spiked to 1.2s for the llama — is that likely from garbage collection or batching issues?
[06:54] Ethan: it could be batching thresholds and tail scheduling; we'll pull the logs. we also saw a small memory reclaim event on one node that caused a transient increase — action item for me to export P99 traces to you.
[07:05] Maya: ok let's recap decisions and next steps. decisions: pin meta-llama-2-13b@v1.3.2 as pilot primary, use mistral-7b at 10% canary, keep gpt-jr-quant as fallback for low-latency routes. pre-warm Dedicated fallback pool and run perf on 2025-03-12.
[07:22] Samir: agreed.
[07:24] Maya: action items recap: Ethan to send full benchmark sheet and P99/P95 traces; Maya to send pricing addendum and security pack; Lena to deliver final prompt set. target dates on the action items are in the notes.
[07:36] Priya: ok thanks — can you also include steps for forced rollback test so we can rehearse incident response?
[07:42] Ethan: yes we can schedule a staged rollback drill during the perf run. we'll document the rollback playbook and include it in the runbook.
[07:50] Maya: awesome, we'll follow up with calendar invites for the perf run and canary monitoring setup. thanks everyone, talk soon.
[07:56] Samir: thanks all.

Optional notes:
Summary: Weekly POC sync focused on final model selection and operationalization of model pinning + fallback strategy. Decision to pin meta-llama-2-13b@v1.3.2 as primary with mistral-7b canary (10%) and quantized gpt-jr fallback. Plan to pre-warm Dedicated fallback pool and run a perf + rollback drill on 2025-03-12.
Topics: model selection, pinning, compatibility maps, quantization tradeoffs, fallback pre-warm, caching, security (KMS, SSO, EU residency), rollout policies and rollback drills.
Links referenced: Benchmark spreadsheet (link shared in chat), Security pack (link to security docs), Runbook template (link).
